backendShape.briefQuote: §8 "Vercel for both web surfaces (the owner is the only admin user; there is no scale case for splitting hosting)."
backendShape.reason: One deployable with two route groups, not two tiers. Public surface is read-mostly ISR with exactly one public write (BookingRequest); admin is dynamic behind a single-account cookie session; the scheduled job is one authenticated route platform cron pulls. Splitting apps/api adds a second deploy target, a second env surface, a cross-origin session-cookie problem and a Dockerfile/compose pair, and buys nothing the brief asks for.
skips: apps/api/Dockerfile — no applicable per-stack template; not emitted
docker-compose.yml — no second service, and the DB is managed (Neon) not a local container
dev.mjs runs ONE process on :3000; no api port, no second health wait
backendShape.moduleBoundary: §9's modules survive as apps/web/src/server/<module>/ with service + route handler; a route handler may only call its own module's service.

integrations.rationale: Rule 0 — brief specifies in-house. §5 'The admin is not a CMS'; §9's seven-keys-cannot-be-created is an API-level refusal Sanity can only express as editor convention.
Rule 0 — one account, no registration, no OAuth, no MFA signal (§9, §13). Argon2id + httpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie + rate-limited login ≈150 lines.

Rule 1 — §8 names it. Rule 4 — Resend Free (3,000/mo, 100/day) is the only free tier covering BOTH lanes at this scale. Port+adapter: project owns send(to,template,data); dev captures to disk, tests mock.

Rule 1 — §8 asks for ONE provider across both lanes. §5's lane separation is preserved in-project: Subscriber table is system of record; the suppression gate runs in the broadcast port BEFORE the adapter, so §9's 'never sent to again by any code path' is mechanically true.

Rule 0 — nothing to buy. SPF include + provider DKIM CNAMEs + self-authored DMARC (p=none, rua=) on a dedicated sending subdomain so newsletter reputation cannot contaminate the apex domain. §8 makes this BLOCKING.

Rule 0 — §12 'Her branding is the template, not an option' is a requirement to REMOVE a capability; committed code states that as architecture rather than policy. React Email (stack is TS/React; renders to string server-side so §17 tests need no runtime; ships no tracking pixel).

Rule 3 + rule 4 — all candidates sit behind one in-house port, so the choice is only the deploy adapter. R2: 10GB free, zero egress, no upload cap (vs Supabase Storage 1GB / 50MB max, which a PDF workbook can exceed) and keeps the S3 API so it swaps without rewrite. EU jurisdictional restriction set.

Rule 0 — forced by the requirement. Crop-to-ratio is generic; the palette treatment that makes a phone snapshot belong to the plum-and-gold world is bespoke and no vendor ships it (§12, §13). sharp/libvips, processed ONCE at upload.
Rule 1 — §8 names it. §7's ISR-with-revalidation and §18's E2E-against-preview both depend on Vercel behaviour. Functions pinned to lhr1 beside the Neon London instance.

Rule 1 — brief-named. Rule 3 breaks the Neon/Supabase tie: Neon is plain Postgres pg_dump moves; Supabase's value is the bundle (RLS/Auth/Storage) this project deliberately does not use. Decisive: Neon's pooled/HTTP driver survives serverless connection churn. AWS eu-west-2 London.

Rule 0 — in-house logic, platform trigger. §8 'Platform cron is sufficient; there is no queue worth running at this scale.' Route is ordinary authenticated HTTP so the trigger swaps to GH Actions or a Worker in one line.

Rule 0 + rule 2 — §13 demands a method not depending on eyesight or JS, which DISQUALIFIES every widget challenge (Turnstile recorded disqualified so this is not silently re-derived). Honeypot + signed time-trap + server validation + Postgres rate limiter + §14 double opt-in.

Rule 0 — the DB is already in the request path and transactional. A rate_limit(key,window_start,count) upsert satisfies §13 without a second datastore, bill and failure mode. Swept by the same cron that expires holds.

Rule 0 — structural, not preferential: one of §11's five block types (upcoming-offerings) is a LIVE DATA REFERENCE, not text, and needs a custom node in any rich-text model. §12 means the editor must not offer formatting control anyway.

Rule 1 — §8 is literal: 'platform error reporting plus uptime checks… No custom dashboards.' The one thing you cannot build is an external vantage point. Healthchecks.io added on a separate §13 signal: nothing else detects a cron that silently stopped firing — the expiry route pings it as a dead-man's switch.

notes: uk-gdpr — lawful basis differs per purpose: contract-steps for a BookingRequest, consent for the newsletter. Never bundled; a booking form may not carry an implied newsletter opt-in.

Residency is designed: Neon AWS eu-west-2 (London), Vercel functions lhr1, R2 EU jurisdictional restriction. Resend sending region eu-west-1 (Ireland) — but Resend ACCOUNT METADATA remains US-hosted, so a DPA is required and the privacy notice must name a US processor for email delivery.

pecr — consent explicit, unbundled, unticked, with evidence (source + confirmed_at) on the subscriber row. Every issue needs one-click unsubscribe, sender identity and a valid postal address. brief §20 Q10 (postal address) is UNRESOLVED and is a hard blocker on the first issue.

Suppression list is owned absolutely (§9); the gate sits in the broadcast port ahead of the vendor adapter so it survives a vendor swap. Unsubscribed addresses are retained indefinitely BECAUSE suppression is the control — document that basis or it reads as a breach.
Booking-request retention 24 months is RECOMMENDED but unconfirmed by the client — needs an operator decision before launch. Implement as a deletion sweep on the existing cron.
no-cookie-consent holds ONLY while the site ships no analytics/advertising cookies. The admin session cookie is strictly necessary and exempt. Any analytics vendor later makes a banner mandatory.
wcag-2-2-aa verified by COMPUTED contrast, not eyeballed — plum ink on blush pool, and #D8BFC9 secondary on the near-black plate. Admin controls count; the owner uses them too.
Unsubscribe tokens non-expiring (one-click must work from a two-year-old email); opt-in confirmation tokens expiring. Both signed server-side, neither guessable from an address.

warnings: VERCEL HOBBY IS NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY — she sells sessions, so Hobby's terms exclude this. Budget Vercel Pro $20/mo. Not optional, and it unblocks two brief requirements: Hobby cron fires at most DAILY (useless for §13 hold expiry needing ~15-min granularity) and Hobby log retention is 1 hour vs 1 day on Pro, which is the whole of the 'platform error reporting' the monitoring pick leans on.
SELF-GENERATED SECRETS APPEAR IN NO INTEGRATION'S credentialsRequired — see projectGeneratedSecrets. Omitting them is the most likely way this architecture ships broken.

IMAGE UPLOAD IS WHERE THE SERVERLESS SHAPE BITES — Vercel request bodies cap ~4.5MB and a sharp resize of a phone photo is memory-hungry. Do NOT POST the file through a route handler: presigned R2 PUT → browser uploads direct → process route streams it back, re-encodes, writes derivatives, deletes the raw. Build it this way from task one; retrofitting after a 413 is far more expensive.

PRISMA + SERVERLESS — pooled string for DATABASE_URL, unpooled DIRECT_DATABASE_URL for migrations. PrismaClient as a module-scope singleton guarded on globalThis in dev or Next's HMR exhausts the connection ceiling within minutes of admin work.

RESEND FREE IS 100/DAY, NOT PER SEND — a newsletter past 100 confirmed subscribers silently fails at the cap. The broadcast port must chunk and record per-recipient send state so a partial issue resumes rather than double-sends.

SENTRY WAS DECLINED, NOT OVERLOOKED — §8's sentence is the smallest that satisfies the requirement and rule 1 says the brief wins. Reconsider the moment a bug outlives Vercel's log retention or the fix-loop needs a production stack trace. Author the captureError port NOW with a no-op adapter so adopting Sentry touches one file.

backend_framework IS NULL DELIBERATELY — every downstream stage (/skills-audit --scope=build, /pm, Dockerfile+compose emitters, dev.mjs) must take the SKIP path, not a default. If a compose.yml or apps/api Dockerfile appears in this scaffold, that is the bug-118 regression: delete it, do not fill it in.

PM MUST NOT SCHEDULE backend-builder — with no backend stack skill it has nothing to dispatch to and fails on lookup. Server-tier tasks belong to web-frontend-builder under react-next. Note it in tasks.yaml so a re-plan does not reintroduce it.
The newsletter postal address (brief §20 Q10) is unresolved and legally required before the first issue sends. Surface it at the gate-5 drop alongside the API keys — it blocks the same milestone.
